It should be clear at this point that certifications are proof of competency. Competency is demonstrated by meeting the education requirements for a degree, diploma or occupational certificate too. So why are additional certifications necessary???
An agency certification example is a General Radiotelephone Operator License (GROL). The certification is awarded by a government agency to qualified individuals.

Trade certifications will be covered later in depth, but a Microsoft Certified Systems Engineer (MCSE) is a good example of a trade certification. Its not a license to work in the local area, but a person must have the certification to be in the occupational field...

Local certification is based on geo-political requirements in the local area. For example, let's assume that in order to perform a fiber optic installation in Austria, workers must have a state telecommunications license. This is a local certification requirement...
Certification has 3 distinct levels: LOCAL, TRADE, and AGENCY.

The certification process is not the receipt of a diploma. Certification starts during the education process and ends when training is required to move up to the next higher rating. Certification standards usually require a candidate to have some amount of practical experience...

From high school graduate to PhD is all part of the education process in the career path. Perhaps education is the career path. A person may want the PhD because the goal is a teaching position at a university. Education may substitute for training, but the reverse is not necessarily valid...

Doctors are certified teachers. A Telecom Doctor would probably be employed by a government agency, university, or scientific research consortium. Telecom PhDs are earned in engineering, networking, or management concentrations...

The loftiest educational goal is the PhD (Philosophiae Doctor) in Telecommunications. A few institutions worldwide offer PhD sponsorship and support. PhD curricula is not structured the same as a post-graduate degree. A doctor is a scientist and an inventor...

The Bachelor of Science degree used is the example is a technology type degree. In other words, it is not highly specialized. The student spends 4 years learning the most important parts of the science...

Military schools enter into partnerships with local civilian institutions. As a result, some military schools are fully accredited and are authorized to award occupational certifications...

The military provides excellent training opportunities and strongly promotes a college education. A large percentage of the professionals in telecom have a military background. The military approach to training is fast paced and vigorous. Military personnel are expected to use their new skills in life and death situations.....

Occupational certificates are earned at trade schools, colleges, and training institutions. The curriculum is highly specialized. A certificate is a certification for the lower entry-level skills.

High school is the starting point of the education process. Adult schools and even the various prison systems offer high school level courses. Some trade-oriented high schools, like those in industrial areas, offer technical courses...

All of the educational institutions should be accredited, meaning valid and respected by authoritative bodies in government and the education community. Do not confuse education and training. Education is a comparatively lengthy process...

The education process is categorized into the following levels: High School * Occupational Certificate * Military Training * Associate in Applied Science * Bachelor of Science * Master of Science * Doctorate of Science/PhD (Philosophiae Doctor)
Doctorate of Science/PhD (Philosophiae Doctor)
Find a mentor to help you move up. Know someone at the next step in the process. Your network of acquaintances should include people at all levels of the career path.

A person's career path cannot be mandated. People set and attain goals based on personal ambition. Some are content to work at the entry level indefinitely. Others change careers mid-stream. Likewise, others return to the path after retirement. The career path process is the only constant...

Training is the process that keeps professionals up-to-date as the technology advances. Training also opens opportunities for branching into other specialties in the industry. If a different specialty is sought through training, a recertification process is required...

The education starts the cycle. When education is complete, the person is ready to be initially placed in the entry level of the industry. If the person is already educated and certified, placement will be at the professional level...

The career path concept is not new or unknown. All professionals know what to do. It is a continuous ladder. The number of repetitions through the cycle is determined by the span of the working life...

An engineer is a highly technical individual with at least a 4 year college degree, who is qualified to design processes, real and/or virtual...

A sales person may pay a visit to the CLEC to finalize a deal. The sales person had better be ready to receive a bombardment of technical questions.....
